method: Complex body harmonics from low-Attack hits, then bounded full-hit pitch/envelope/DC fitting after 11 ms and a joint low/high Attack fit for the first 30 ms including the native LPF. Full-hit fit numerical outputs are retained; calibrate.py reproduces the complex harmonic and initial differential-pulse stage, not all subsequent optimizations.

implementedModel._about: Private Analog BD 909 reference candidate, revision AB014REF03. Fit to Skee Mask’s supplied 70 BPM recordings, including complex body harmonics and full-hit envelope/DC. The supplied audio report identifies a decay-modified 909, decay a little above halfway, knob changes after hits and occasional final endpoint repeats. Physical intermediate knob positions remain unknown.

tune._tune0: Both endpoint excursions and exponential time constants are fitted to complete measured hits. Intermediate nodes remain a monotone design interpolation; the recording is not treated as uniformly spaced physical knob positions.
tune.base_delta_note: Difference between steady-tail fits of the first four and final four Tune recording hits; intermediate settled-pitch shift follows the excursion interpolation. Separate capture drift is not synthesized as random pitch.

body.c_note: Complex H1-H16 fit from Attack hits 2..13. A degree-11 even-phase polynomial plus u*(1+x) times a degree-4 quadrature polynomial matches temporal asymmetry; DC, gain, hold/droop and coupling fit complete low-Attack hits after 11 ms. Envelope opening and crest hold are retained model choices.

pulse._note: Long and fast discharges both follow ATK. Joint low/high fit includes the native LPF and complete body model. Input gains divided by 16 and filter gains multiplied by 16 preserve headroom; the mixer also retains its quarter scale. Coupling and output poles reached upper bounds; values describe a fitted model, not measured component constants. jitter_* vary strength, never timing.

mackie._note: SAT / LOW / HIGH: a Mackie-desk stage after the 909's output, with airwindows MackEQ (Chris Johnson, MIT) as the reference, not a port: its clip + x - k_sat x^5 curve at the input, in the bass and high bands and at the output stage, its band drive law 4u^2 and its one-pole crossover coefficients, and its output stage 9 dB (stage) above its input stage. Unlike MackEQ the split is complementary and each band's output is sqrt(2u), so LOW 64 / HIGH 64 is flat and SAT 0 is transparent (-75 dB from dry on the init patch).
mackie.rise_note: Unpadded RMS (0-300 ms, init patch, LOW/HIGH 64) above SAT 0, measured on the float design; the make-up table holds the rise to target_rise_db at SAT 127.
mackie.hp_note: The desk's input is AC-coupled (MackEQ's k_hp, ~13 Hz at 44.1 kHz); without it the 909's DC thump, times SAT's drive, pins the input stage and leaves a DC shelf after every hit. Its coefficient ramps from 0 at SAT 0 (DC-coupled, the calibrated 909) to k_hp at SAT hp_full, so the knob has no step.

limits: Endpoints also informed fitting; their error measures fit quality, not independent validation.
Coupling/output pole bounds are model choices, not measured circuit constants.
Decay mapping outside the recorded modified-909 setting retains the existing curve.
Physical intermediate knob positions are unknown; control interpolation remains a design choice.
scope: Historical AB014REF04 body/Tune/whole-hit fit. Its pulse coefficients and minimum-pulse gain are superseded by direct-out-fit.json; body and Tune values remain current.
